chapitres.reperer: Finding your way around the app

couverture.sous: StreamOS — your streaming control room, made simple.

principe.p1: StreamOS is your control room: the **large central area** (dashboard) is where you lay out your stream. **OBS** then shows the result to your viewers.
principe.p2: StreamOS **drives OBS Studio** for you: simply start OBS (**preferably first**) and everything syncs by itself. Your OBS scenes are **never modified** — StreamOS just adds its own source next to yours.
principe.l1: **Dynamic and interactive** scenes: one game or fifty, switching is smooth, with or without a Stream Deck — and everything is **saved**, widget by widget, down to the app background.
principe.l2: **Decorative frames** regularly added, giving depth to your stream.
principe.l3: Import your **media** in a snap, tilt them in **3D**, shape them to your liking.
principe.note: Move or resize an element: the render in OBS updates **live**.

premierPas.p1: **Three settings** are all it takes to be stream-ready.
premierPas.e1: In OBS: Tools menu → **WebSocket Server Settings** → enable the server and note the port (**4455** by default) and the password.
premierPas.e2: Here, in the sidebar's **OBS** section: enter the port and the password, then **Connect**.
premierPas.e3: On first launch, pick a **scene template**: everything is already laid out for you.
premierPas.e4: Connect your **chat**: Twitch and YouTube ask for a code to validate online; Kick and TikTok connect with just a username.
premierPas.note: Scene templates remain available anytime via the "**+ Scene**" button at the top.

obs.p1: The sidebar's **OBS** section changes color by itself: **red**, StreamOS can't see OBS; **green**, everything is in place.
obs.l1: "**OBS is unreachable**": OBS isn't open, or its WebSocket server is off. Open OBS, then Tools → **WebSocket Server Settings** → check "Enable WebSocket server".
obs.l2: "**Password missing or invalid**": in that same window, click "**Show Connect Info**", copy the password and paste it here.
obs.l3: The **Host** field keeps its default value as long as OBS runs on the same computer.
obs.p2: Once connected, the **Start stream** and **Start recording** buttons become active in the same section.
obs.note: No OBS yet? The "**Download OBS Studio**" link at the bottom of the section opens the official page.

modeles.p1: On first launch, the "**Welcome to StreamOS**" window offers ready-to-use scenes. One click, and widgets, frame and positions are set for you.
modeles.l1: **Gaming** (and its 4:3 and fullscreen variants): game capture, camera, chat, keyboard or gamepad.
modeles.l2: **Just Chatting**: large camera on the left, chat on the right.
modeles.l3: **Speedrun**: splitter on the left, chat on the right, keyboard at the bottom.
modeles.l4: **Minimal**: a discreet chat and a thin frame — all the room for the game.
modeles.p2: Everything stays editable afterward. To build it all yourself, choose "**Start from a blank page**".
modeles.note: A scene template **never** replaces an existing scene: it is added next to it.

cartes.p1: A **left click** on any element in the central area opens its card at the top of the left side panel: a clearly visible dotted box gathering everything that element allows.
cartes.intro: The dotted line's color changes depending on the clicked element:
cartes.p2: A **right click** on a widget opens a context menu made of simple shortcuts (duplicate, reorder, delete). All these options are also found with a **left click**, in its card in the left side panel.
cartes.note: The card closes by itself when nothing is selected anymore — another click and it's back.

barreLaterale.p1: Everything is driven from the **left panel**. Only one section opens at a time; the others are simple buttons that open a window.
barreLaterale.l1: **Widgets**: create a widget (media, chat, camera, input viewer, speedrun, goal, music).
barreLaterale.l2: **Connections**: Twitch, YouTube, Kick, TikTok — a green dot per connected platform.
barreLaterale.l3: **Live interactions**, **Waiting screen**, **Just Chatting**, **Channel**, **Diagnostic**: the stream control windows.
barreLaterale.l5: **Preview**: miniature of what your viewers see.
barreLaterale.l6: **Personalization**: frames and background image. At the very bottom, the **Streamer's guide** (this book) just above **Ergonomics**: dashboard background, window and shortcuts bar.
barreLaterale.note: Each open section takes its card's color: blue for Widgets, green for Connections, gold for OBS…

scenes.p1: The top bar lists **your scenes**. Click "**Your scenes**" to unfold them, then a name to open it: the broadcast switches instantly.
scenes.l1: "**Scene**" creates a new scene, from a template or a blank page.
scenes.l2: A **right click** on a scene: **Rename**, **Duplicate**, **Show / Hide title**, **Delete**.
scenes.l3: **Drag** a scene to change its order in the bar.
scenes.l4: Deletion always asks for confirmation — nothing is lost by accident.
scenes.note: Each scene keeps its own widgets, background and frame: switching between them never mixes anything.

plateformes.p1: The sidebar's **Connections** section. Each row has its dot: grey = disconnected, green = online.
plateformes.l1: **Twitch** and **YouTube**: click **Connect**, a code appears — enter it on the indicated web page, that's it. No password is ever typed into StreamOS.
plateformes.l2: **Kick**: type your channel name (as it appears in the kick.com/… address) then **Connect**.
plateformes.l3: **TikTok**: type your username then **Connect**. The live must be running.
plateformes.l4: **YouTube**: the **Chat ON / Chat OFF** button pauses chat reading without disconnecting.
plateformes.p2: On the next launch, StreamOS **reconnects by itself** to the platforms already linked.
plateformes.note: An error message appears under the list if a connection fails: it tells you what to do.

chat.p1: **A single chat widget** gathers messages from all your connected platforms: create it via "**Create a chat widget**" in the **Widgets** section of the left panel, or directly by picking a **scene template** that already includes it.
chat.l1: **Twitch, YouTube, Kick and TikTok** in the same feed, each message with its logo.
chat.l2: Each platform's **viewer count** is shown at the top of the widget.
chat.l3: If a platform drops, **reconnection happens by itself**.
chat.p2: Two styles in its card: **Compact** (messages stack inside the widget) or **Bubbles** (the widget disappears, viewer counter included — each message floats alone, bigger, dressed in the frame).
chat.note: TikTok connects by username, no account — handy, but the protocol is **unofficial**: a temporary outage can happen.

widgets.p1: **Place, move and resize** each widget with the mouse, right in the central area.
widgets.l1: To show your game: enable the widget's **capture window**, then "**Link an OBS source**" — pick the game or app, StreamOS does the rest.
widgets.l2: Move the capture window: the OBS capture **follows it on its own**, no setup.
widgets.l3: The camera is cut to the **shape of the chosen frame** — circle, hexagon…

medias.p1: An image, a video, a logo: **drag the file** from your computer onto the "**Drop your .PNG here or images/video**" strip at the bottom of the central area. A media widget appears instantly.
medias.l1: From a media widget's card: "**Replace media**" or "**Delete media**".
medias.l2: Several images at once → "**Create a carousel**": they cycle at the chosen **interval**.
medias.l3: For the scene background: a **left click on the background** then "**Import a background**" — or "**Set an app/game as background**".
medias.note: **.mkv** videos are converted automatically on import — nothing to do on your side.

carteEdition.p1: The card that opens on a **left click** on a widget is organized in tabs. Every setting applies **live** to the broadcast.
carteEdition.l1: **Content**: what is displayed — media, chat filter and style, camera device, input viewer mode… and this widget's frame.
carteEdition.l2: **Transformation**: the 3D compass to tilt the widget, the media **Display** (fit, fill, stretch…), **Zoom**, **Rotation** and offset.
carteEdition.l3: **Effects**: brightness, contrast, hue, blur, pixelation, **Mirror**, and morphing (**Grow / Shrink** by clicking the media). A **Reset** button per tab puts everything back flat.
carteEdition.note: A video adds the **Playback** tab; every widget has the **Duplicate** tab (a mirrored copy, ready to align).

cadres.p1: **A single setting** dresses all your widgets and the scene border: same style, same color, everywhere.
cadres.p2: Open the Frames modal from the sidebar's **Personalization** section: the chosen model applies live to the broadcast.
cadres.note: Alerts and banners automatically reuse the **active frame's colors**.

cadresModale.p1: Nine styles to choose from — Rounded, Square, MGStyle, Cyberpunk, Story, Thin Line, Hexagon, Arena, Tribal — each with its color and thickness.
cadresModale.e1: Sidebar → **Personalization** → "**Your frames**". Click a style in the gallery: the preview updates.
cadresModale.e2: Adjust the **Thickness** and the color **Gradient**. Enable "**Animation**" if you want the gradient to move.
cadresModale.e3: Click "**Frame enabled**": it applies to all your widgets. "**App border**" adds the same frame all around the broadcast.
cadresModale.note: A widget can be an exception: in its card, "**Remove frame from this widget**".

alertes.p1: Sidebar → "**Live interactions**". This window gathers everything that reacts to your viewers during the stream.
alertes.l1: **Alerts** tab: follow, raid, sub, resub, gift sub, bits (Twitch) — plus TikTok gifts, Kick subs/raids and YouTube SuperChats/members. Pick a type on the left, then its media, its text, and enable it. "**Test the alert on the broadcast**" plays it without waiting for a real follow.
alertes.l2: **Welcome clip** tab: a clip played when a follower arrives in chat. "**Auto-assign**" gives everyone a clip; you can also pick the clip by hand, viewer by viewer.
alertes.l3: **Position skeleton** tab: drag the overlay where you want it on screen — the position applies to alerts, clips and commands.
alertes.note: Everything plays on the **OBS broadcast**, never in the dashboard: use the Preview to check.

bandeau.p1: A banner highlights each viewer's **first message** in your chat, across all platforms. A way to say hello to every newcomer.
bandeau.e1: **Live interactions** → **First message banner** tab → check "**First message banner enabled**".
bandeau.e2: Choose **Top** or **Bottom** of screen and the **display duration** (2 to 20 seconds).
bandeau.e3: "**Test the banner**" shows a fake banner on the broadcast to check the render.
bandeau.note: New stream? "**Reset session**" makes all viewers "first" again — otherwise a regular never retriggers the banner.

attente.p1: Taking a break? The waiting screen shows a **media** or an **animated decor** with a **countdown**, on the broadcast only. Your dashboard stays free.
attente.e1: Sidebar → "**Waiting screen**". Import a media, or keep the **StreamOS signature** or **Minimal** style.
attente.e2: Set the **timer duration** and place the timer and title by dragging them in the preview.
attente.e3: Click "**Launch the waiting screen**". To come back: "**Resume**".
attente.note: If your media has sound, check "**Sound enabled**": StreamOS handles the audio routing in OBS.

justChatting.p1: Feel like chatting without the game? The "**Just Chatting**" button in the sidebar switches the broadcast to **camera + chat only**, in one click.
justChatting.p2: Nothing is modified in your scene: click again, everything comes back exactly as before. The green dot shows the mode is active.
justChatting.note: The mode is **off at every StreamOS startup** — no bad surprise when launching the stream.

previsualisation.p1: The **Preview** section shows a **live miniature** of the broadcast: exactly what your viewers will see.
previsualisation.l1: Choose **Windowed** or a **Monitor**, then "**Open projector**": OBS opens a large preview on the chosen screen.
previsualisation.l2: A click on the miniature does the same thing.
previsualisation.note: The camera and game captures do **not** appear in the miniature (they are rendered by OBS) — they do show in the projector.

demarrer.p1: All set? The stream launches **without leaving StreamOS**.
demarrer.e1: **OBS** section: click "**Start stream**". The dot turns green, the button becomes "**Stop stream**".
demarrer.e2: To keep a local copy: "**Start recording**", independent from the stream.
demarrer.e3: At the end of the session, the same buttons stop both.
demarrer.note: The **Start streaming** button in the top bar does the same thing, always at hand.

plusLoin.p1: The main tour is done. The rest is discovered in the app, each window explaining what it does.
plusLoin.l1: **Channel**: Twitch and YouTube moderation — ban, VIP, moderators, stream title and category, ads, shield mode.
plusLoin.l2: **Live interactions** → **Commands**, **Numpad**, **Presentation**, Twitch **Schedule**, **Music** requested by your viewers with "!rs".
plusLoin.l3: **Goal** widgets (followers, subs…), **Speedrun** (chrono splitter), **Input viewer** (keyboard, mouse, gamepad on screen).
plusLoin.l4: **Diagnostic**: StreamOS CPU and memory usage, live.
plusLoin.l5: **Ergonomics** → **shortcuts bar**: a small bar always visible, even over the game.
plusLoin.l6: The **language** selector at the top: the app speaks eight languages.

fin.p1: The rest is discovered section by section in the **sidebar**: connections, widgets, personalization… **Happy streaming!**
